## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

Rural and Metro Totals by Quarter
```{r}
# Create the data frame
totalsbyq <- data.frame(
  quarter = c("Quarter 1", "Quarter 2", "Quarter 3", "Quarter 4"),
  metro = c(3575538, 3277365, 5321291, 4999835),
  rural = c(6158765, 7134395, 7521307, 6909484)
)

# Convert relevant columns to a matrix (excluding the 'quarter' column) and scale by millions
totals_matrix <- as.matrix(totalsbyq[, c("metro", "rural")]) / 1e6

# Grouped Bar Plot
bar_positions <- barplot(t(totals_matrix), 
                         main = "Rural and Metro Total Services by Quarter",
                         xlab = "Quarter", 
                         ylab = "Number of Services (in millions)", 
                         col = c("darkblue", "lightblue"),
                         beside = TRUE, 
                         names.arg = totalsbyq$quarter)

# Add the legend in the top right corner
legend("topleft", 
       legend = c("Metro", "Rural"), 
       fill = c("darkblue", "lightblue"),
       cex = 1, 
       bty = "n")  

```
